newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina encouraged on Falklands by Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Argentina encouraged on Falklands by Hong Kong.

text.p: The imminent handover of the British colony of Hong Kong to China later this year has encouraged Argentina in its sovereignty claim for the Falklands, Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella said.
"It is a very important event for us, Britain withdrawing from a territory that it insisted was unequivocally British," he told Pagina 12 newspaper in an interview published on Tuesday.

Argentina has a 130-year-old claim to the British-run islands in the South Atlantic, which the two countries went to war over in 1982. About 1,000 servicemen died before a British task force defeated Argentine troops sent to the remote, windswept islands to impose the territorial claim.

The two countries have restored diplomatic relations and built up flourishing trade links, but President Carlos Menem insists periodically that Argentina will win back the islands it calls "Malvinas" by the year 2000.
"We have made great advances," Di Tella said. "We are much closer to reaching that point than we believe."
Di Tella called Hong Kong's return to China on June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule "a practical and convenient idea for both sides."
But he said Britain was less likely to hand over the Falklands because their occupants are British.
"The racial element in British policy is very important," he said. "The British have a more emotional relationship with the islands than they would if they were Chinese or creole."

Di Tella said Argentina itself was largely to blame for the islands still being in British hands, because it went to war with Britain just when it was ready to hand over the islands to Argentine rule.
"I don't have the slightest doubt -- if it hadn't been for the war, we would be discussing the details of the handover today," the Argentine foreign minister said.
